summary30s: Article 51 of Directive Principles directs India to promote international peace and security, realized through Nehru's Non-Aligned Movement (NAM, founded at Belgrade 1961).
Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was signed on 29 April 1954 between Nehru and Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai.
The 1959 Tibetan uprising (Dalai Lama's asylum in India) and border disputes in Aksai Chin and NEFA triggered the October 1962 Sino-Indian War, severely denting India's image.
The 1965 Indo-Pak war ended with the Soviet-mediated Tashkent Agreement (Jan 1966); the 1971 Bangladesh War resulted in 93,000 Pakistani PoWs and the July 1972 Shimla Agreement.
India conducted its first nuclear test in May 1974 at Pokhran ('Peaceful Nuclear Explosion') and Pokhran-II in May 1998 under Atal Bihari Vajpayee, committing to 'No First Use'.

coreConcepts.title: Constitutional Mandate & Non-Alignment Policy (NAM)
coreConcepts.explanation: Article 51 of the Indian Constitution lays down the Directive Principle to promote international peace, maintain just relations, and encourage arbitration of international disputes. Nehru shaped Non-Alignment not as neutrality or passivity, but as active, independent decision-making without joining either the US or Soviet military blocs (NATO / Warsaw Pact). Key milestones: Asian Relations Conference (March 1947); Bandung Conference (1955) in Indonesia; First NAM Summit held at Belgrade in September 1961, attended by 25 countries. The five founding leaders were: Jawaharlal Nehru (India), Josip Broz Tito (Yugoslavia), Gamal Abdel Nasser (Egypt), Sukarno (Indonesia), and Kwame Nkrumah (Ghana).
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 4, Section 1 & 2
coreConcepts.examTip: Five founding leaders of NAM: Nehru (India), Tito (Yugoslavia), Nasser (Egypt), Sukarno (Indonesia), Nkrumah (Ghana). First summit: Belgrade (1961).

coreConcepts.title: Peace and Conflict with China: Panchsheel to the 1962 War
coreConcepts.explanation: On 29 April 1954, Nehru and Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai signed the historic Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence): (1) Mutual respect for territorial integrity and sovereignty, (2) Mutual non-aggression, (3) Mutual non-interference in internal affairs, (4) Equality and mutual benefit, (5) Peaceful coexistence. However, relations deteriorated rapidly after China annexed Tibet in 1950. In 1959, following a popular Tibetan uprising, the Dalai Lama was granted political asylum in India. China accused India of anti-China activities. Border disputes flared in two sectors: Aksai Chin in Ladakh and the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA, modern Arunachal Pradesh). In October 1962, China launched a massive surprise attack in both sectors, capturing vital posts before declaring a unilateral ceasefire in November. The debacle led to the resignation of Defence Minister V.K. Krishna Menon and the first No-Confidence Motion against the Nehru government.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 4, Section 3
coreConcepts.examTip: Panchsheel was signed on 29 April 1954. Defence Minister V.K. Krishna Menon resigned following the 1962 war defeat.

coreConcepts.title: Wars with Pakistan: 1965 (Tashkent) and 1971 (Shimla)
coreConcepts.explanation: In April 1965, Pakistan launched an attack in the Rann of Kutch (Gujarat), followed by Operation Gibraltar in August-September in Jammu and Kashmir. Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the famous slogan 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan' and ordered Indian troops to open a counter-offensive towards Lahore. Hostilities ended with the UN ceasefire, and in January 1966, Shastri and Pakistani President Ayub Khan signed the Tashkent Agreement, mediated by Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin. Shastri tragically passed away hours later in Tashkent. In 1971, Pakistani military atrocities under General Tikka Khan in East Pakistan triggered an influx of 1 crore Bengali refugees into India. In August 1971, India signed a 20-year Treaty of Peace and Friendship with the USSR. In December 1971, Indian armed forces and Mukti Bahini defeated Pakistan in 13 days; on 16 December 1971, General A.A.K. Niazi surrendered with 93,000 troops at Dhaka, creating Bangladesh. On 3 July 1972, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto signed the Shimla Agreement, resolving to settle all disputes bilaterally.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 4, Section 4
coreConcepts.examTip: Tashkent Agreement (Jan 1966): Shastri & Ayub Khan (Soviet mediation); Shimla Agreement (July 1972): Indira Gandhi & Z.A. Bhutto (bilateralism).

coreConcepts.title: India's Nuclear Policy: Pokhran-I (1974) to Pokhran-II (1998)
coreConcepts.explanation: India's nuclear program was initiated in the late 1940s under Dr. Homi J. Bhabha. India opposed the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) of 1968, criticizing it as discriminatory because it legitimized the monopoly of the 5 permanent members of the UN Security Council while denying nuclear technology to others. In May 1974, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi conducted India's first nuclear test at Pokhran (Rajasthan), designated as a 'Peaceful Nuclear Explosion' (PNE). In May 1998, Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee conducted a series of five nuclear tests at Pokhran (Operation Shakti), establishing India as a declared nuclear-weapon state. India formulated a credible minimum nuclear deterrence policy with a strict 'No First Use' doctrine, pledging never to use nuclear weapons against non-nuclear states.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: Politics in India Since Independence, Chapter 4, Section 5
coreConcepts.examTip: Pokhran-I: May 1974 (Indira Gandhi); Pokhran-II: May 1998 (Atal Bihari Vajpayee). India refused to sign NPT (1968) and CTBT (1996) as discriminatory.

workedExamples.question:
The historic Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence) was signed on 29 April 1954 between which two leaders?
(A) Jawaharlal Nehru and Zhou Enlai
(B) Jawaharlal Nehru and Mao Zedong
(C) Lal Bahadur Shastri and Ayub Khan
(D) Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto

options.text: Lal Bahadur Shastri and Ayub Khan
Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto

workedExamples.explanation: The joint communique signed on 29 April 1954 by Indian Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru and Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai contained the Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence (Panchsheel).
solutionStepByStep: Step 2: Signatories: Nehru (India) and Zhou Enlai (China).

workedExamples.question:
Who mediated the Tashkent Agreement signed in January 1966 between Indian Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri and Pakistani President Ayub Khan?

workedExamples.explanation: The Tashkent Agreement was mediated by the Soviet Union. Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin brought Lal Bahadur Shastri and General Ayub Khan together at Tashkent in January 1966.
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Recall the mediator of the 1966 Tashkent conference.
Step 2: Alexei Kosygin, Prime Minister of the USSR.

commonTraps.misconception: Assuming India signed the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) in 1968.
commonTraps.correctConcept: India vehemently REFUSED to sign the NPT (1968) and the Comprehensive Test Ban Treaty (CTBT, 1996) because they established a discriminatory nuclear monopoly for the P-5 nations.
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Questions ask whether India is a signatory to the NPT.
commonTraps.cuetWarning: India has NEVER signed the NPT or CTBT.

commonTraps.misconception: Confusing the Shimla Agreement (1972) with the Tashkent Agreement (1966).
commonTraps.correctConcept: Tashkent (1966) resolved the 1965 War (Shastri & Ayub Khan, mediated by USSR); Shimla (1972) resolved the 1971 War (Indira Gandhi & Z.A. Bhutto, bilateral without third-party mediation).
commonTraps.whyTrapWorks: Students swap the signing Prime Ministers and years.

practiceQuestions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India contains provisions for the 'Promotion of international peace and security'?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Article 51 of the Constitution under Directive Principles directs the State to promote international peace and security.

practiceQuestions.question: In which year and city was the First Summit of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) held?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The first summit of the NAM was held in Belgrade in September 1961.

practiceQuestions.question: Who was the Defence Minister of India who resigned taking moral responsibility for the military debacle in the 1962 Sino-Indian War?
practiceQuestions.explanation: V.K. Krishna Menon, the then Defence Minister, resigned from the Union Cabinet following the defeat in the 1962 war.

practiceQuestions.question: The Shimla Agreement was signed on 3 July 1972 between Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and which Pakistani leader?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The Shimla Agreement was signed by Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto on 3 July 1972.

practiceQuestions.question: In August 1971, facing the looming Bangladesh crisis and the US-China-Pakistan axis, India signed a 20-year Treaty of Peace, Friendship and Cooperation with which superpower?
practiceQuestions.explanation: In August 1971, India signed the 20-year Treaty of Peace and Friendship with the Soviet Union.

practiceQuestions.question: In which year did India conduct its first nuclear test at Pokhran under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi?
practiceQuestions.explanation: The first nuclear explosion undertaken by India was in May 1974.

practiceQuestions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the five founding leaders of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)?
practiceQuestions.explanation: Mao Zedong was not a founder of NAM. The five founders were Nehru, Tito, Nasser, Sukarno (Indonesia), and Nkrumah (Ghana).

practiceQuestions.question: Why did India refuse to sign the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) of 1968?

options.text: Because it banned nuclear power plants for electricity generation
Because it was discriminatory, legitimizing nuclear weapons for five countries while denying them to others
Because Pakistan had already signed it
Because the United Nations did not recognize Hindi as an official language

practiceQuestions.explanation: India considered the NPT as discriminatory and refused to sign it because it divided the world into nuclear 'haves' and 'have-nots'.

practiceQuestions.question: The spiritual and temporal leader of Tibet who sought and was granted political asylum in India in 1959 was:
practiceQuestions.explanation: In 1959, the Dalai Lama crossed over into the Indian border and was granted asylum.

practiceQuestions.question:
Given below are two statements, one labelled as Assertion (A) and the other labelled as Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Following the 1998 Pokhran-II nuclear tests, India adopted a nuclear doctrine of 'No First Use'.
Reason (R): India's nuclear posture commits to credible minimum deterrence while assuring that India will not initiate a nuclear attack against any adversary.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: India formulated a nuclear doctrine emphasizing 'No First Use' and maintaining only minimum credible deterrence. Both are true and (R) explains (A).
